name: Kraken
description: Kraken is the most competitive and high-stakes variant of the Dutch national game Klaverjassen. Played by four players in two partnerships, it follows the standard 'Amsterdamse' rules but adds an aggressive bidding and doubling system ('Kraken'). In this version, the opponents can 'crack' a contract if they believe the makers will fails to win half the points, doubling the round's value. It is the preferred variant of serious Dutch Klaverjas players.

history.origins: Developed in the mid-20th century in Amsterdam as a way to increase the psychological depth of Klaverjassen. The term 'Kraken' (to crack) refers to the act of challenging the contract-maker.
timeline: 1910s: Klaverjassen becomes the Dutch national card game.
1950s: Kraken variant emerges in competitive cafe leagues.
Present: The standard format for professional tournaments in the Netherlands.
history.cultural: Commonly played with a 'Goudse' or 'Amsterdamse' deck in Dutch coffee houses (bruine cafÃ©s).
history.evolution: Transitioned from a leisurely social game to a high-tension bidding game where understanding your partner's 'roem' (melds) in hand is crucial.

setup.deck: 32 cards (7 through Ace). The Jack of Trumps (20 pts) and Nine of Trumps (14 pts) are the highest.

rules.objective: Win more than half of the total points (usually 81+ out of 162 total card points) plus roem.
rules.gameplay: Must follow suit. If unable, you MUST trump. If a trump is led, you must overtrump (Amsterdamse rules).
keyRules: Must follow suit; if unable, must trump. If trump is led, must overtrump (Amsterdamse rules).
After trump is chosen, opponents may say Kraak (contra) to double; makers may herkraken to quadruple; opponents may superkraken to octuple.
Roem in hand is claimed before the first trick; the team with the highest single combination scores all its roem; the other team scores none.
The side that announced the last kraak must take more than half the points to win; the winning side takes all points (multiplied by kraaks).

strategy.basic: Prioritize the Jack and Nine of trumps. Without at least one of these two cards, your team is extremely vulnerable to being 'Cracked'.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Compulsory Lead': Since the first player must pick trumps, they should pick their strongest suit even if it's mediocre. If they hold zero trumps, they must pick a suit where they have high Aces to defend against a Kraken.
strategy.advanced: Roem Detection: Watch your partner's first lead. If they lead a card that looks unusual (like a 7 or 8), they might be signaling a void or a high sequence ('Roem') in their hand.
tips: Only 'Crack' if you hold at least the Trump Jack or the Trump Nine. If you have neither, the makers will likely fulfill their contract.
Capturing the last trick is worth 10 points. In a 'Cracked' game, this becomes 20, 40, or 80 points!
